title: Unusual instruments: a piccolo player and balloon blowing
summary: Punch recalls a piccolo player and a dance where he was asked to blow up balloons.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Did they have any hard instruments that played with the jazz bands? Hard instruments? Hard instruments, unusual instruments in those times.
I don't know nothing but a fella come up to us one night with a piccolo.

Oh, he left here in Chicago too. But I think he's from Mobile, his name was Jackson, some kind of Jackson, Earl Jackson or William Jackson, something. Throw the thing on the side, you know. So we kept him playing one night, and he played it too. And I tried and I got, this is Dizzy's name, ooh, that thing on the Dizzy. I'll never forget a man named Jenkins. He used to have all that old gravel and stuff, you know, Peoples to wake from him. And he gave a big, big dance for the night. And by me getting there early, he told me to blow up some balloons. And he's going to give us something blowing balloons up. Man, I blow six of them things up, you know what I mean? Yeah. All right, well, it's just a song that I made about back in the old days of New Orleans. It seems to me that some fella came here from foreign country, you know, and met me on the street. And he said, now look here, Pront. He said, I'm here in town now. And he said, what I heard at my home, I don't see it here. I heard about how the people used to do here years ago. But I don't see that yet. Well, could you explain to me some of the things that happened years ago? And then, you know, I'll go to sing the song plan. Well, I'll make the end of this. You want me to make the end of this one?
